propositions: On platforms without /proc (macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and causing an unbounded lock wedge when a dead process's pid is reused by an unrelated live process.
The lock is incorrectly judged fresh when a live-pid verdict is unqualified (current_start unavailable), bypassing the 1h stale ceiling that governs all other unprovable cases.

A live owner holding both fcntl and mkdir legs cannot be reclaimed by the ceiling check because reaching that line requires already holding the exclusive fcntl leg, which a genuine owner would still possess.
On the live-pid branch, when current_start is None, apply the stale ceiling check; preserve immediate reclaim for known-and-differing start times and never-reclaim for matching start times.
The owner-identity/stamp/staleness/reclaim cluster is extracted from lock.py (798 LOC) to lock_owner.py to comply with the 800 LOC module-size limit.
